TECHNICAL TERMS
3.1
INTRODUCTION
Just like there are numerous things around us and every thing has its own particular name
which facilitates its use, all the things ~
in cutting and tailoring too have their own name.
These names have a particular meaning in the trade. Hence, for anyone entering the world
of cutting and tailoring, it becomes essential to be familiar with the terminology,
But before we learn the technical terms, let us learn what is the need for having technical
terms and also the advantage of using such terms in our work day like.
3.2
OBJECTIVES
After reading this lesson, you will be able to do the following:-
•
describe technical terms used in cutting and tailoring;
•
use these terms in your work.
3.3
WHAT ARE TECHNICAL TERMS?
Words associated with a particular trade and which have a certain meaning relevant to the
trade are called technical terms. These terms are extensively used in that particular trade.
3.4
NEED
1)
To accomplish the work easily and conveniently.

2)
To save time
3.5
ADVANTAGES
1)
These are easily understood
2)
It becomes easy to communicate with others.
3.6
SOME TERMS YOU SHOULD KNOW
1.
Grain
Lengthwise or crosswise threads of a fabric. The lengthwise grains are called
'weft' and the crosswise grains are called 'warp' or 'woof.
2.
Grainline
The lengthwise threads show the grainline.
3.
Bias
A strip of cloth cut at an angle of 45° to the lengthwise and widthwise grain is
known as 'bias' or bias strip. It has maximum stretch.
4.
Seam
The line of stitching obtained onjoining two pieces-of fabric is known as a 'seam'.
5.
Base line
The line on which drafting begins is known as 'base line'.
6.
Facing
Any strip offabric used to finish an edge is known as 'facing', e.g. in necklines and
armholes. Sometimes facings are not turned in but turned out onto the right side
of a garment in a decorative manner.
7.
Opening
The open parts of a garment made to facilitate putting on and taking off are known
as 'openings'.
8.
Slit
The side opening in a garment is known as 'slit'.Both the edges of a slit touch each
other but do not overlap. Example-slit in coatjackets, slit in kurta in ladies salwar
suit.

Technical Terms :: 31
9.
Gathers
When the width of fabric is reduced to desired width by pulling it tight into small
ruffles is known as 'gathers'. This may be done by running a wide stitch on the
machine or by tacking by hand and then pulling up the thread to from the gathers.
10.
Inlays
The extra fabric kept outside the seam line of a garment is known as 'inlays'.
11.
Margin
While cutting, the extra fabric kept apart from that needed according to
measurement is known as 'margin'. This is usually kept so that the seams can be
let out and the garment expanded, if needed, later on.
12.
Hem
When the desired length of any garment is to be finished, the extra cloth is folded
in and secured with a fine hand stitch known as 'hem'.
13.
Laying
The laying out of the cloth before cutting is known as 'laying'.
14.
Layout
The markings made on the laid out cloth according to the pattern are called 'lay
out'.
IS.
Lining
The layer of cloth used under the cloth of the garment is known as 'lining'. Lining
is used in fine and delicate fabrics (silks) in woolen cloth (in coats) under rough
fabrics and under transparent fabrics like organdy.
16.
Inter lining
Any cloth used between the cloth of the garment and the lining cloth is known as
'interlining'. Example 'buckram'.
17.
Balance mark
The different pieces of a garment are marked in order to keep a balance during
stitching. These marks are known as 'balance marks'.
18.
Turning
The section of cloth which is turned inside to finish the length of any garment is
known as 'turning'. This can be let out to increase the length of the garment.

32 :: Home Science
19.
Turn up
Sometimes the turning is turned up onto the right side of the garment. This is
known as 'turn-up' .
. 20.
. Finishing
The trimming of allextrathread aftercompletion ofa garmentisknown as'finishing'.
21.
Locking of seam
Securing the beginning and end ofseam is known as 'locking of seam'.
22.
Button stand
When buttons are fixed to a thick edge as in a coat, the button is not fixed not
flat onto the edge but some length ofthread is left between the button and the
garment surface. This length ofthread is known as a 'button stand'. It allows the
two thick edges to close comfortably without tightening ofthe button.

23.
Flap
The piece of cloth attached to cover the top of a pocket is called a 'flap'.
24.
Velt
Velt is the piece of original cloth used to make the opening of a cut pocket.
25.
Warp
The lengthwise threads in a fabric are called 'warp'.
26.
Weft
The widthwise threads in a fabric are called 'weft'.
27.
Paper pattern
After the drafting is made, it is transferred to a paper according to the actual
measurements ofthe gahnent. This is known as 'paper pattern'.
28.
Depth of syce
The depth ofthe armhole is called 'depth of syce'.
29.
Arm hole
The opening for the ann is known as 'ann hole'. It is the place where the sleeve
of the garment fits in.

Technical
Terms :: 33
30.
Try
When the garment is made by tacking and tried on for size and fitting, it is called
'try'.
31.
Damp cloth
While pressing woolen garments a soft moist cloth is placed over the garment and
then pressed. This cloth is called 'damp cloth'.
32.
Trimming
Any material used to decorate a garment like lace, beads, ribbons, etc. is know
as 'trimming'.
33.
Leg shape
The shape ofthe inner leg below the crotch is called 'leg shape'.
34.
Placket
Any opening in a garment which has an overlap is called a 'placket'. Plackets
usually have some means of closing like a zip, button with holes or hooks with
eyes, etc.
35.
Alteration
Changes made in a garment to remove fitting defects.
36.
Selvedge
The lengthwise edge of a fabric is called 'selvedge'.
37.
Stud
The upper portion of a press button is called 'stud'.
38.
Tacking
Tojoin two pieces of cloth with long, uneven stitches, preparatory to final stitching
is called 'tacking'.
39.
Sleeve head
The top round portion of a sleeve is called 'sleeve head'.
40.
Renovation
To give a new look to an old garment is called 'renovation' .

34 :: Home Science
41.
Flair
The loose, round part of a garment is called 'flair', as in a skirt or sleeve.
42.
Jetting
The piece of cloth used to cover the edge of a pocket in order to cover the lining
is called Jetting piece'.
43.
Gorge
The roundness of a neckline is known as 'gorge'.
44.
Iron speaking
The hissing sound made when a very hot iron comes in contact with water is
known as 'iron speaking'.
